system:
You label an inbound customer tweet sent to a streaming service's support handle with exactly one intent from this taxonomy.

playback_error: The stream fails to play: buffering, freezing, blank screen or an error code. Cues: "error code 300", "keeps buffering".
device_app_issue: The app itself is broken, crashing or missing features on a named device or platform. Cues: "app crashes on my Roku", "not working on my smart TV".
login_access: Cannot sign in or reach the account: password, email, verification or lockout. Cues: "can't log in", "password reset link never arrives".
billing_subscription: Money or plan: charges, refunds, trials, upgrades, downgrades, cancellation. Cues: "charged twice", "how do I cancel".
ads_complaint: Ads or commercials: too many, repeated, or shown on a plan the customer pays to avoid. Cues: "I pay for no commercials", "same ad five times an episode".
content_availability: A specific title, season or episode the service normally carries is missing, removed, mislabelled or wrong (audio, subtitles, order). Cues: "episodes disappeared", "the subtitles are for the wrong episode".
content_request: Asks to add a title, season, channel or league the service does not carry. Cues: "please add season 3", "when will you get NBC".
product_feedback: Opinion or request about the product itself, including feature requests such as shuffle, skip-intro, mark-as-watched, playlists, interface changes. Cues: "the new interface is terrible", "please add a skip intro button".
feature_question: Asks whether, when, where or how something works or is available: a device, region, plan, setting or release timing. Cues: "will it be on tonight", "does it work in Canada".
praise_or_thanks: Compliments, thanks, or friendly chatter with no request for support. Cues: "thanks for the quick help", "love the new lineup".
other: Anything else: unclear, off-topic, empty or not about this service. Cues: "hey guys", "<link>".

Examples:
playback_error <- getting error code 300. What is this & how can we get it fixed??
playback_error <- been trying to watch and it keeps buffering... tried everything.
device_app_issue <- app is still not working on my smart tv. I've reset multiple times and nothing
device_app_issue <- why does new iPhone app show black screen when connected to Apple TV?
login_access <- I have been trying to cancel my HBO trial for over a week but can't access my account!
login_access <- password reset email never shows up, I am locked out
billing_subscription <- I canceled hulu but was charged. How do I get that back?
billing_subscription <- Just upgraded to no commercials, how do I downgrade again?
ads_complaint <- at which time should there be ads in past programming when you pay for no ads?
ads_complaint <- Why do I have to pay for Hulu and have to watch commercials?
content_availability <- why are my favorite shows all saying not available right now??
content_availability <- Alias series 1-5 was removed last night while I was half way through
content_request <- when is season 3 of rick and morty coming
content_request <- Hulu Team please add Bein sports to live TV line up.
product_feedback <- Your slick new interface makes browsing and discovery more difficult.
product_feedback <- the new iPad platform is terrible!!
feature_question <- is there a way to enable 5.1 sound on one
feature_question <- do you have a free trial so I can compare Hulu Live with my current subscription?
praise_or_thanks <- thanks so much, that fixed it!
praise_or_thanks <- It's so good, loving the new lineup
other <- hey guys
other <- <link>

Answer with JSON only: {"intent": "<name>", "confidence": <0-1>}
user: I got an email to verify my account by Dec 1 or my account would be terminated. is this legit?
text:
I can't verify the specific email since I don't have access to it, but I can help you spot red flags. This pattern—**urgent deadline + threat of account termination + "click to verify"**—is a very common phishing tactic. Here's how to check it yourself:

**Red flags to look for in the email:**
- **Sender address**: Check the *actual* domain (not just display name). Legitimate companies send from their real domain (e.g., `@netflix.com`), not lookalikes (`@netflix-support.com`, `@netfliix.com`, etc.)
- **Generic greeting**: "Dear Customer" instead of your name
- **Urgency/threats**: Real companies rarely threaten termination with a hard countdown like this
- **Link mismatch**: Hover over (don't click) any button/link — check if the URL actually matches the company's real domain
- **Spelling/grammar errors** or unusual formatting
- **Requests for sensitive info**: passwords, full card numbers, SSN, etc.

**Safest way to confirm:**
1. **Don't click any links in the email.**
2. Open the service's app or type the official website URL directly into your browser.
3. Log in normally and check if there's actually a verification notice or account warning in your account settings.
4. If concerned, contact the company's official support channel (from their real website, not the email) and ask them directly.

If you want, tell me which service the email claims to be from (e.g., Netflix, Hulu, Disney+, etc.) — I can tell you what their legitimate domains/support channels look like so you can cross-check.
